transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired another top general.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reports Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia has been forced out of a key war planning post.
Several U.S. officials confirmed to NPR that Gen. Sylvia was fired from his position
as head of strategy plans and policy for the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
At first the Pentagon put out a statement thanking Gen. Sylvia for his 32 years of distinguished service.
But that statement is being pulled back because the Pentagon is investigating the general for allegedly leaking to the media.
Gen. Sylvia served several tours in Iraq and Afghanistan where he received medals, including for valor.
He and his family have in the past been the target of right-wing influencer Laura Loomer.
Hegseth has accused senior advisers of leaking in the past, but none of them have been court-martialed or prosecuted.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
Alaska's Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola is dismissing a New York Times report.
It alleges her campaign was part of efforts to put another Senate candidate on the ballot
with the same name as Alaska's incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.
That recruit is retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan.
Dan J. Sullivan, not the incumbent senator, denies this.
Alaska Public Media's Liz Ruskin reports Mary Peltola did not directly refute the Times report.
Republicans have alleged for months that the second Sullivan is a Democratic plant intended to draw votes away from the senator.
The Times story seems to substantiate that claim, although NPR has not independently confirmed that reporting.
Peltola dismissed the story as a distraction.
Nobody at the New York Times cares about affordability in Alaska.
Super PACs often promote spoilers in Alaska elections.
The state's ranked choice voting method is intended to blunt the spoiler effect.
But not all voters rank their ballots.
For NPR News, I'm Liz Ruskin in Anchorage.
Meanwhile, Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy has ordered an investigation into the matter based on the New York Times reporting.
But the Alaska State Supreme Court ruled in June that the second Sullivan, Daniel J. Sullivan,
could appear on the ballot along with the incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan.
The Alaska Court ruled nothing in state or federal law allowed it to rule on the motives of a candidate.
The federal government says the U.S. economy grew 3.4 percent between July and September.
At the same time, Americans are struggling with inflation and things that are costly are just not affordable.
A separate report today says that inflation in the U.S. in September accelerated 3.6 percent compared to one year ago.
You're listening to NPR.
Spanish officials say at least 69 people were killed in yesterday's collision of two trains. They are still investigating the crash scene in central Spain.
A new study estimates that three quarters of NFL players who died over the last 20 years had a neurodegenerative brain disorder that is linked to suffering blows to the head.
And Fiar's John Stoleness has more.
The study out this week looked at the player's age, cause of death, mentions of dementia, years of NFL experience, and even positions played.
The conclusion? Three out of four players likely would have had some level of chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE, in their brains had autopsies been conducted.
Back in August, researchers from Boston University, Mass General Brigham, and the Concussion and CTE Foundation examined the donated brains of nearly 400 former players and found one in four who died between 2016 and 2021 had CTE.
The new analysis by the same researchers sought to expand their findings to the nearly 2,000 players who died between 2008 and 2023 whose brains were not donated.
John Stoleness, NPR News.
Game six of the WNBA Finals will be held in a little more than an hour.
The Atlanta Dream will host the Golden State Valkyries. The Valkyries lead the series three games to two.
There's been frustration. All three Atlantic games have had to be rescheduled to accommodate last minute adjustments that did not seem to be anticipated by the WNBA.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Pentagon fires Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia from Joint Chiefs strategy post amid leak investigation
Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola dismisses New York Times report on rival Dan J. Sullivan ballot effort
Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy orders investigation into New York Times reporting on second Sullivan candidate
U.S. economy grew 3.4 percent from July through September, federal government reports
U.S. inflation accelerated to 3.6 percent in September compared with a year earlier
Spanish train collision kills at least 69 people in central Spain, investigation continues
Study estimates three-quarters of deceased NFL players had neurodegenerative brain disorder linked to head blows
Atlanta Dream to host Golden State Valkyries in WNBA Finals Game Six
